references.title: الغُرْبةُ
references.rights_note: Arabic Academy dictionary defines الغربة in the relevant sense as النوى والبعد (separation/distance). Public wording is an original synthesis and does not reproduce long source text.

references.title: Home in exile: Palestinianness as moral subjunctive destination
references.rights_note: Ethnographic analysis distinguishes ghurba as an affective experience of exile/estrangement, loss, longing and not-belonging; Palestinian context is a direct studied population, not a license to generalize to all Arabic speakers.
references.citation_display: Schiocchet, L. (2024). Home in exile: Palestinianness as moral subjunctive destination. HAU: Journal of Ethnographic Theory, 14(1). https://doi.org/10.1086/729840

references.title: غُرْبَة — Arabic pronunciation
references.rights_note: Arabic IPA /ɣur.ba/ used for research. Product audio still requires exact file/creator/locale/license/SHA verification.

references.title: hiraeth
references.publisher_or_container: Geiriadur Prifysgol Cymru (University of Wales Dictionary)
references.rights_note: GPC is the standard historical Welsh dictionary. The hiraeth entry is used as the lexical authority; a Cambridge scholarly chapter reproduces its broad definition of grief, longing, nostalgia, homesickness, wistfulness and desire for what might have been.

references.title: Hiraeth and Ambiguous Pastorals: Wales, England and Rural Modernities between the Wars
references.rights_note: Scholarly chapter quotes the GPC lexical definition and situates hiraeth historically. Cultural discussion is used as context, not as proof of a timeless Welsh national character.
references.citation_display: Hiraeth and Ambiguous Pastorals: Wales, England and Rural Modernities between the Wars. (2021). Cambridge University Press.

references.title: hiraeth — Welsh pronunciation
references.rights_note: Welsh North/South IPA variants are recorded. The research record uses a standard North Wales form [ˈhɪraɨ̯θ]; product audio remains unverified.

references.title: viraha
references.rights_note: Monier-Williams lexical sense: abandonment, desertion, parting, separation especially of lovers, absence. Scholarly rasa/bhakti sources are required for the experiential love-in-separation framing.
references.citation_display: Monier-Williams, M. (1899). viraha. A Sanskrit-English Dictionary.

references.title: The Cloud of Longing: A New Translation and Eco-Aesthetic Study of Kalidasa's Meghaduta
references.rights_note: Scholarly eco-aesthetic study treats viraha as separation/loss and shows longing amplifying the mood of separation in Sanskrit poetics. Public copy must preserve the classical aesthetic boundary.
references.citation_display: Jarow, E. H. R. (2021). The Cloud of Longing. Oxford University Press.

references.title: viraha — Classical Sanskrit research pronunciation
references.publisher_or_container: Monier-Williams / standard Classical Sanskrit phonological reconstruction
references.rights_note: Research IPA [ʋi.ɾɐ.ɦɐ] follows Classical Sanskrit segment values and IAST viraha. This is not a verified product recording; product pronunciation/audio remains HOLD.
references.citation_display: Cologne Digital Sanskrit Lexicon. (n.d.). Monier-Williams Sanskrit-English Dictionary.

references.title: tampó
references.rights_note: Filipino lexical entry defines tampo through showing sama-ng-loob/displeasure, usually through silence and distancing from others.

references.title: Understanding Apos as an Emotional Language among Young People in a Commercial Farming Landscape
references.rights_note: Ethnographic study links Kankanaey apos with Filipino tampo as a deep-seated emotional/relational idiom expressed through withdrawal; culturally encouraged repair/assuagement is observed in the studied community and must not be universalized.
references.citation_display: Sidchogan-Batani, R. (2021). Understanding Apos as an Emotional Language among Young People in a Commercial Farming Landscape. The Cordillera Review. https://doi.org/10.64743/EMIV5158

references.title: tampo — Tagalog pronunciation
references.rights_note: Standard Tagalog IPA /tamˈpo/ is used for research. Product audio requires exact source-file rights verification.

references.title: querencia
references.publisher_or_container: Diccionario de la lengua española, RAE-ASALE
references.rights_note: RAE defines affection/loving, the tendency to return to a place where one was raised or habitually goes, and the place toward which such querencia is felt. Human-emotion card must fence animal/bullfighting senses.
references.citation_display: Real Academia Española. (n.d.). querencia. Diccionario de la lengua española.

references.title: El valor emocional de la experiencia paisajística. Querencias y paisajes afectivos
references.rights_note: Peer-reviewed geography paper examines emotional landscape experience and querencias/affective landscapes. Used to support place-affect framing, not to replace the RAE lexical boundary.
references.citation_display: Puente Lozano, P. (2012). El valor emocional de la experiencia paisajística. Querencias y paisajes afectivos. Cuadernos Geográficos, 51, 270–284.

references.title: querencia — Spanish pronunciation
references.rights_note: Spanish IPA variants are recorded; the research record uses Spain /keˈɾenθja/. Product audio remains unverified.

screened_out.reason: Romanian dor is culturally and semantically rich, but ordinary Korean 그리움/향수 already covers much of the central longing/nostalgia sense. Keep for direct comparison rather than priority admission.
Turkish hüzün has substantial literary/cultural scholarship, but basic lexical sadness/melancholy is close to Korean 슬픔/우울/애수 and distinctiveness can easily be manufactured by cultural essentialism.
